text: {"contradictions":[{"source":"Iure igitur plectim.","english":"Rightly, therefore, are we punished.","kind":"role","why":"The Latin 'plectim' (plectimur) is passive, but the context of the argument implies the subject is the Roman people/state being punished by the gods/fate, whereas the English 'we' implies the speaker and audience are the agents of their own punishment.","certainty":"medium"},{"source":"du hoies pdia hasta illa crues ta et meminerme t sperabur.","english":"when men have remembered those bloody spears and hoped for them.","kind":"sense","why":"The Latin 'sperabur' (sperabantur) is passive ('were hoped for'), but the English translates it as active ('hoped for them').","certainty":"high"},{"source":"du mes tui. q. cari esset diligi maluimus.","english":"if we preferred to be loved when we wished to be dear.","kind":"sense","why":"The Latin 'cari esset' (cari esse) means 'to be dear', but the English reverses the logic of the comparison between being loved and being dear.","certainty":"medium"}],"omissions":[],"additions":[]}

contradictions.why: The Latin 'plectim' (plectimur) is passive, but the context of the argument implies the subject is the Roman people/state being punished by the gods/fate, whereas the English 'we' implies the speaker and audience are the agents of their own punishment.

contradictions.source: du hoies pdia hasta illa crues ta et meminerme t sperabur.
contradictions.english: when men have remembered those bloody spears and hoped for them.
contradictions.why: The Latin 'sperabur' (sperabantur) is passive ('were hoped for'), but the English translates it as active ('hoped for them').

contradictions.source: du mes tui. q. cari esset diligi maluimus.
contradictions.english: if we preferred to be loved when we wished to be dear.
contradictions.why: The Latin 'cari esset' (cari esse) means 'to be dear', but the English reverses the logic of the comparison between being loved and being dear.
